analysis.answer: Currently, no law addresses religious displays in public school classrooms. This measure creates a mandate requiring an 11 by 14 inch poster of the Five Pillars of Islam in every public school classroom.

Direct costs include the production, distribution, and installation of the posters for every public school classroom. There are also likely to be significant legal costs for the state and local districts to defend the mandate against constitutional challenges.
Public school districts, and ultimately taxpayers, will bear the financial burden of procuring the posters and defending potential litigation.

Schools will need to source and mount the posters to comply with the mandate. Civil liberties and religious freedom organizations are likely to file lawsuits seeking injunctions against the requirement, arguing it violates the Establishment Clause of the First Amendment.
The text asserts no specific problem it is trying to address, but functions to introduce religious displays into public school classrooms.
The state legislature gains control over specific classroom displays, removing discretion from local school boards, principals, and teachers regarding this wall space.
Assuming this is a statutory measure, it can be undone by passing a new law repealing the mandate or if a court strikes it down as unconstitutional.
